To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the RCA gene cluster is organized into two TADs with an intragenic inter-TAD boundary and is co-regulated via enhancer elements.

1) the regulatory architecture of the RCA locus is highly complex, comprising multiple gene-gene and long-range enhancer-gene interactions; 2) CTCF-mediated looping and TAD formation is a key feature of the RCA locus, with the inter-TAD domain boundary located at a segmental duplication; and 3) we identified a novel, long-range enhancer that upregulates CR2 and CD55, two key susceptibility genes in complex genetic diseases.
